reconstruction: Families were classified as confidently present (P ≥ 0.95), confidently absent (P ≤ 0.05) or unresolved, rather than split at 0.5, which assigns every unresolved family to one side. Equal rates was prespecified for the primary reconstruction. An all-rates-different model was fitted for comparison: it is uninformative for 1,006 of the 1,245 families, returning a marginal probability near 0.5 at the stem, and among the 239 for which it is informative it gives a different confident classification from equal rates for 112. Among the families underlying the clade-wide loss set it agrees with equal rates for 23 of the 53, is confident alongside equal rates for 30 and makes an opposite confident call for 12. The stem assignment is therefore model-dependent and the counts reported are the equal-rates result.

Scale of reduction: gene families versus gene copies (SPIRE MAGs, Prodigal CDS)

FSM-RGM difference, computed on the 96 FSM and 97 RGM annotated MAGs: mean 3,359 CDS in FSM against 5,787 in RGM, a difference of 2,428 CDS over a mean genome-size difference of 2.41 Mb (about 990 bp per missing gene). Cluster-level accounting: 2,919 CDS per genome from clusters absent from FSM, plus 829 from gross positive differences in clusters both clades retain, minus 1,319 from clusters enriched in FSM, summing to the observed 2,428. On a carrier-conditioned basis the shared-cluster difference is mostly prevalence (about 167 CDS) rather than copies among carriers (about 60). Supersedes the earlier median-based statement of a 2,575-CDS shortfall with 393 absent families and 2,182 additional copies.
Within-family copy-number contraction: functional composition of the 200 largest losses
Contraction is spread over 3895 clusters totalling 829 CDS per genome; the 200 largest account for 23% of that total; no small set of families dominates.
